question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Order of an Ordinary Differential Equation
question.problem: What is the order of the ordinary differential equation $y\frac{{\text{d}}^{4}y}{\text{d}{x}^{4}}-4{x}^{2}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=2x?$
question.worked_solution:
The order of an ordinary differential equation (ODE) is the order of the highest derivative in the equation.

The highest derivative in the given ODE is $\frac{{\text{d}}^{4}y}{\text{d}{x}^{4}},$ which has order $4.$

Therefore, the order of the ODE is $4.$

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, the order of the ODE is $4.$
